body:
My second experience with cookies involved no other people. The previous time i was with 6 others and some damn wierd shit happend, so i decided to try it alone 'cause I was curious about its potential for meditation. I sat alone in a sun-lit, calming room and closed my eyes as if trying to sleep. I came up (as you do), and  was intent on controlling the experience, and contentrating on particular internal sense experiences. I was buzzing uncontrolably like an attomic powered dildo but realized that I could switch the feeling of euphoria off whenever I opened my eyes to the room. My perception of the room - which looked the same as it had always done - brought me back in touch with the world, but with eyes closed I could walk around the corridors of my mind; it was if I was in two worlds: my internal one, and the external (the 'real') one. Because I was able to switch between the euphoric state and a normal analytic 'realist' state I was able to analise the euphoric sensation in me.
The conclusion I drew from the eupthoria aspect is that this is what it must feel like when someone claims to be in the presence of God. I felt a warm externally induced sense of belonging and secturity, as if some almighty being was surounding me and protecting me. I felt as if I was not alone.
I now belive God to be nothing more than an electro-chemical reaction inside our brains that makes us feel safe and warm and just  generally splendid. When felt in someone not under the influence, it would probably be at a time in their lives when they are faced with something almost imposible deal with (i.e. the death of a loved one). So, this seratonin safety valve clicks in, they interperate the sensation as God, and they are 'saved' from having to deal with the shittyness of reality.
I would love to do a blood sample on some one who has just this second claimed to have found God - I'm sure the same brain chemicals and functions that happen whilst on E are in effect.
